extensions.reviewLimits: Code reconciliation only. Device tests and finish review are handled separately in docs/validation.md and review records. This record does not certify exact game fidelity, performance, field navigation, or freedom from clipping. Missing approved comp and FORM seed are not invented.

rendering.mapLifecycle: Welcome does not create MapView. Hidden map rendering is paused/stopped and update effects are inactive; route state is preserved.
rendering.previewCaching: MapSwatch builds batched building, street and route paths with drawWithCache; all onDrawBehind painting is enclosed by clipRect to contain it within the preview bounds. World list rows have stable keys.
rendering.nativeMapFonts: Bundled SDF ranges selected by World.mapFontName(), resolved by MapGlyphs.kt; missing ranges fall back to provider Noto Sans. Internal Waypoint Classic stack is a font identifier, not a world.
rendering.compassMeaning: Reliable phone sensor heading or GPS course; not map bearing.
rendering.attribution: Compact labelled Map info control opens provider links in a native dialog.
rendering.welcomeLaunch: Ordinary fresh launches show welcome despite an in-memory selected place. Active guidance and external destination launches bypass welcome.
rendering.headingEmissions: The heading arbiter retains samples while covered. UI emissions pause unless the map or sensor settings is visible, or the car display is visible. Resuming publishes the current reading. With reliability, source and status unchanged, changes below 0.3 degrees are suppressed.
rendering.mapControls: AtlasTool: 64dp-wide, minimum 70dp column plus 4dp gutter, 48dp icon plate. PixelSlot: 64dp-wide with 56dp sprite plate. Both use the single-line control-caption token. Location caption: Locate.
rendering.compassTypography: Cardinal: 15sp/18sp standard or 20sp/24sp ornate. Degrees: 11sp/14sp. Zero tracking.
rendering.previewToolbar: Back, ROUTE, Worlds and Settings sit on the selected theme panel backing and shape above the route-preview card.
rendering.routeFooterActions: End trip and Steps are 64dp wide with minimum 64dp height and 2dp content padding. Roboto Condensed captions use 12sp/16sp, zero tracking, a single line and no soft wrapping.
rendering.routePreviewViewport: onGloballyPositioned measures map, header and destination-panel bounds in root pixels. MapViewportInsets derives the unobscured viewport with 28dp breathing room and system-inset handling: the middle between panels in portrait, or below the left toolbar beside the panel in compact landscape. Fitted bounds include route points, actual GPS origin and selected destination. Overview bearing and tilt are explicitly zero: north-up and flat, independent of the idle world camera. Fitting waits for usable measured insets and reruns when measured layout/insets or style change; there is no fixed pixel-padding assumption. This is a code description, not device validation.
rendering.compactDestination: Normal portrait: 16dp padding, 12dp gaps, Material titleLarge, up to two address lines. Compact height: 12dp padding, 8dp gaps, titleMedium, one address line; destination names permit two lines in both. Compact preview uses a horizontal Locate action with minimum 48dp height instead of the vertical icon/caption control.
rendering.destinationSaveAction: Save/Saved is 64dp wide with minimum 56dp height and 2dp content padding. Roboto Condensed caption: 12sp/16sp, zero tracking, one line, no soft wrapping.
rendering.adaptiveLauncherIcon: Original arrow, bent route and open compass brackets; 108dp vector layers with the mark scaled 0.88 around (54,54). Android owns masking and themed monochrome tint. Full-color map texture belongs only to the background layer. This launcher identity does not replace game palettes.
rendering.destinationSearch: Native Place or address field with keyboard Search and visible Search places button, enabled at two trimmed characters. Submission hides the keyboard. Selected-world shape and place accent are retained. Rows show a two-line place name, three-line address, separate provider attribution and optional distance. Plus-Code-only Android responses explicitly say Address result for … and Android geocoder · address match.

narrative.overview:
Waypoint makes real navigation feel like a game atlas. The map occupies the main surface; controls borrow the selected game's composition, lettering, material and marker grammar. The user's confirmed direction is: “Keep each game's distinct control layout, but polish it.” Consistency comes from touch sizing, legibility and behavior, rather than identical control positions.

This records the implemented Android system, not a claim of exact game reproduction. The app uses authored graphics, licensed substitute fonts and real geographic data. Reference screenshots remain research evidence. Search, settings and destination flows retain native Android conventions; the atlas is the expressive surface.
keyCharacteristics: Distinct map compositions for 27 game worlds; no general-purpose Classic choice.
Game-specific cartography, materials, pointers and place markers.
An animated native welcome screen, uniform world-card naming hierarchy and visible control captions.
Native touch targets and readable navigation data.
Actual streets, GPS state and route progress rather than invented gameplay.

rules.name: The Route Separation Rule
rules.body: Road, route and selected destination must remain distinguishable in the selected world. Map color changes do not justify hiding street connectivity.

rules.name: The Paired Contrast Rule
rules.body: Choose foreground and panel as a pair from the world palette. For text directly over the map, use the explicit light or dark treatment of that atlas instead of inheriting a panel foreground blindly.

rules.name: The Lettering Identity Rule
rules.body: Preserve the selected world's display character while keeping native form text and route details readable. Do not turn every game into the same terminal or pixel font.

rules.name: The Card Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Every launcher and picker card puts the map-style name at 22sp with 28sp line height, and the game name beneath at 12sp with 17sp line height. Keep this scale uniform while retaining each style's typeface.

rules.name: The Distinct Layout Rule
rules.body: Keep the game-specific idle composition. Improve spacing and reachability inside that composition before moving controls into a common shell.

rules.name: The Visible Action Rule
rules.body: Map icon actions need short visible captions as well as semantic descriptions. Use Search, Locate, Worlds, Settings, Map tilt, Mute or Sound on rather than requiring users to infer the icon alone.

rules.name: The Reliable Heading Rule
rules.body: Show direction only when the sensor/course selection is reliable. Use the unavailable state instead of a frozen or fabricated bearing, and do not substitute map rotation for the live heading.

dos: Do preserve the selected world's layout, material and lettering while improving contrast and spacing.
Do keep real roads, route guidance and the position marker legible together.
Do retain native touch targets, semantic labels, insets and system navigation behavior.
Do consult the actual map or navigation state in `docs/visual-sourcebook.md` before changing a theme.
Do show only reliable phone heading or travel course in the compass, with a dash when unavailable.
Do keep world-card title sizes uniform and visible captions on map icon controls.
Do retain native scrolling, cached preview paths and paused hidden map rendering.
donts: Don't reduce all themes to one shared layout with changed colors.
Don't reintroduce a non-game world or cancel navigation when changing a world.
Don't add invented health, money, missions or other gameplay data to navigation.
Don't distort geography or hide roads to imitate fictional terrain.
Don't treat posters, cinematics or decorative treasure maps as interchangeable with navigable map references.
Don't describe substitute fonts, authored materials or mobile adaptations as exact proprietary game assets.
